title: Chapter 2 – Sāṅkhya Yoga (The Yoga of Knowledge)
subtitle: Yoga of Knowledge

verses.title: 2.1 tam tatha kripayavishtam
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच ।
तं तथा कृपयाविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् ।
विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥ २-१॥
verses.roman:
sañjaya uvāca
taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam
viṣīdantamidaṃ vākyamuvāca madhusūdanaḥ 2-1
verses.colloquial:
sanjaya uvaacha
tam tathaa kripayaa aavishtam ashru puurna aakula iikshanam
vishiidantam idam vaakyam uvaacha madhusuudanah 2-1
verses.translation_reworded: Sanjaya said: To Arjuna, who was overwhelmed in this way by pity and despair, his eyes brimming with tears and his mind in turmoil, Madhusudana spoke these words.

verses.title: 2.2 kutastva kashmalamidam
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् ।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥ २-२॥
verses.roman:
śrībhagavānuvāca
kutastvā kaśmalamidaṃ viṣame samupasthitam
anāryajuṣṭamasvargyamakīrtikaramarjuna 2-2
verses.colloquial:
shrii bhagavaan uvaacha
kutas tvaa kashmalam idam vishame samupasthitam
anaarya jushtam asvargyam akiirti karam arjuna 2-2
verses.translation_reworded: The Blessed Lord said: Arjuna, where has this dangerous state come from? This dejection is unworthy of an Aryan; it shuts the door to heaven and brings disgrace.

verses.title: 2.3 klaibyam ma sma gamah
verses.sanskrit:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥ २-३॥
verses.roman:
klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitattvayyupapadyate
kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa 2-3
verses.colloquial:
klaibyam maa sma gamah paartha naitat tvayi upapadyate
kshudram hridaya daurbalyam tyaktvaa uttishtha parantapa 2-3
verses.translation_reworded: Do not give in to weakness, Partha. It does not suit you. Shake off this petty faint-heartedness and rise up, Parantapa (scorcher of foes)!

verses.title: 2.4 katham bhishmam aham
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच ।
कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन ।
इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥ २-४॥
verses.roman:
arjuna uvāca
kathaṃ bhīṣmamahaṃ saṅkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana
iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāvarisūdana 2-4
verses.colloquial:
arjuna uvaacha
katham bhiishmam aham sankhye dronam cha madhusuudana
ishubhih prati yotsyaami puujaarhau arisuudana 2-4
verses.translation_reworded: Arjuna said: Madhusudana, destroyer of enemies, how can I shoot arrows in battle at Bhishma and Drona, men who deserve my worship?

verses.title: 2.5 gurunahatva hi
verses.sanskrit:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्
श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके ।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव
भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥ २-५॥
verses.roman:
gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvān
śreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣyamapīha loke
hatvārthakāmāṃstu gurūnihaiva
bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān 2-5
verses.colloquial:
guruun ahatvaa hi mahaanubhaavaan
shreyo bhoktum bhaikshyam apiiha loke
hatvaa artha kaamaams tu guruun ihaiva
bhunjiiya bhogaan rudhira pradigdhaan 2-5
verses.translation_reworded: It would truly be better in this world to live on a beggar's food than to kill these most honorable teachers. If I kill them, then even here on earth every pleasure of wealth and desire I enjoy will be smeared with their blood.

verses.title: 2.6 na chaitadvidmah
verses.sanskrit:
न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो
यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम-
स्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥ २-६॥
verses.roman:
na caitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo
yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ
yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāma-
ste'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ 2-6
verses.colloquial:
na chaitad vidmah kataran no gariiyo
yadvaa jayema yadi vaa no jayeyuh
yaan eva hatvaa na jijiivishaama-
ste'vasthitaah pramukhe dhaartaraashtraah 2-6
verses.translation_reworded: I can hardly tell which outcome would be better: that we defeat them, or that they defeat us. The sons of Dhritarashtra, whom we would not even want to outlive after killing them, are standing right in front of us.

verses.title: 2.7 karpanya-dosho pahata
verses.sanskrit:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः
पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः ।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे
शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥ २-७॥
verses.roman:
kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ
pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharmasammūḍhacetāḥ
yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṃ brūhi tanme
śiṣyaste'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam 2-7
verses.colloquial:
kaarpanya dosha upahata svabhaavah
pricchaami tvaam dharma sammuudha chetaah
yacchreyah syaan nishchitam bruuhi tanme
shishyas te'ham shaadhi maam tvaam prapannam 2-7
verses.translation_reworded: My heart is crushed by the weakness of pity, and my mind is confused about what my duty is. I am asking You: tell me plainly what is good for me. I am Your disciple. I have taken refuge in You; teach me.

verses.title: 2.8 na hi prapashyami
verses.sanskrit:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्
यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् ।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं
राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥ २-८॥
verses.roman:
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād
yacchokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām
avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddhaṃ
rājyaṃ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam 2-8
verses.colloquial:
na hi prapashyaami mamaapanudyaad
yacchokam ucchoshanam indriyaanaam
avaapya bhuumau asapatnam riddham
raajyam suraanaam api cha adhipatyam 2-8
verses.translation_reworded: I cannot see anything that would take away this grief that is drying up my senses, even if I won a rich and unrivaled kingdom on earth, or even rulership over the gods.

verses.title: 2.9 evam-uktva hrishikesham
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप ।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥ २-९॥
verses.roman:
sañjaya uvāca
evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapa
na yotsya iti govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha 2-9
verses.colloquial:
sanjaya uvaacha
evam uktvaa hrishiikesham gudaakeshah parantapa
na yotsya iti govinda uktvaa tuushniim babhuuva ha 2-9
verses.translation_reworded: Sanjaya said: After saying this to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha, destroyer of enemies, told Govinda, "I will not fight," and fell silent.

verses.title: 2.10 senayorubhayor-madhye
verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥ २-१०॥
verses.roman:
tamuvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasanniva bhārata
senayorubhayormadhye viṣīdantamidaṃ vacaḥ 2-10
verses.colloquial:
tam uvaacha hrishiikeshah prahasan niva bhaarata
senayoh ubhayoh madhye vishiidantam idam vachah 2-10
verses.translation_reworded: O Bharata, to him, despairing there between the two armies, Hrishikesha spoke these words with something like a smile.

verses.title: 2.11 ashochyan-anvashochas
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे ।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥ २-११॥
verses.roman:
śrībhagavānuvāca
aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase
gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ 2-11
verses.colloquial:
shrii bhagavaan uvaacha
ashochyaan anvashochas tvam prajnaa vaadaamsh cha bhaashase
gataasuun agataasuumsh cha na anushochanti panditaah 2-11
verses.translation_reworded: The Blessed Lord said: You are grieving over people who do not deserve grief, and yet you speak as if you were wise. The truly wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

verses.title: 2.12 na tvevaham jatu nasam
verses.sanskrit:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥ २-१२॥
verses.roman:
na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ
na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param 2-12
verses.colloquial:
na tvevaaham jaatu naasam na tvam neme janaadhipaah
na chaiva na bhavishyaamah sarve vayam atah param 2-12
verses.translation_reworded: There was never a time in the past when I did not exist, or when you did not, or when these kings did not. Nor will any of us ever cease to exist in the future.

verses.title: 2.13 dehino smin yatha
verses.sanskrit:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्ति र्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥ २-१३॥
verses.roman:
dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā
tathā dehāntaraprāptir dhīrastatra na muhyati 2-13
verses.colloquial:
dehino'smin yathaa dehe kaumaaram yauvanam jaraa
tathaa deha antara praaptih dhiirah tatra na muhyati 2-13
verses.translation_reworded: Just as the embodied soul moves through childhood, youth and old age in this body, it also moves on into another body. A person of steady mind is not troubled by this.

verses.title: 2.14 matra-sparshas tu
verses.sanskrit:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः ।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्या स्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥ २-१४॥
verses.roman:
mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ
āgamāpāyino'nityā stāṃstitikṣasva bhārata 2-14
verses.colloquial:
maatraa sparshaastu kaunteya shithoshna sukha duhkha daah
aagama apaayino'nityaah staan titikshasva bhaarata 2-14
verses.translation_reworded: Son of Kunti, the meeting of the senses with their objects produces heat and cold, pleasure and pain. These experiences come and go; they do not last. Bear them with courage, descendant of Bharata.

verses.title: 2.15 yam hi na vyathayantyete
verses.sanskrit:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥ २-१५॥
verses.roman:
yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha
samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so'mṛtatvāya kalpate 2-15
verses.colloquial:
yam hi na vyathayanti ete purusham purusha rishabha
samaduhkhasukham dhiiram sah amritatvaaya kalpate 2-15
verses.translation_reworded: The steadfast person who is not disturbed by these things, best of men, and who treats pleasure and pain alike, is ready to realize the immortality of the Self.

verses.title: 2.16 nasato vidyate bhavo
verses.sanskrit:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्त स्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ २-१६॥
verses.roman:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ
ubhayorapi dṛṣṭo'ntas tvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ 2-16
verses.colloquial:
naasato vidyate bhaavo naabhaavo vidyate satah
ubhayor api drishto'ntas tu anayoh tattva darshibhih 2-16
verses.translation_reworded: What is unreal has no existence, and what is Real never ceases to exist. Those who know the Truth (the seers of the Essence) have seen the truth about both.

verses.title: 2.17 avinashi tu tadviddhi
verses.sanskrit:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥ २-१७॥
verses.roman:
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam
vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścitkartumarhati 2-17
verses.colloquial:
avinaashi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idam tatam
vinaasham avyayasya asya na kashchit kartum arhati 2-17
verses.translation_reworded: Understand that what pervades this whole universe is Indestructible. No one can bring about the destruction of That, the Imperishable.

verses.title: 2.18 antavanta ime deha
verses.sanskrit:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः ।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥ २-१८॥
verses.roman:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ
anāśino'prameyasya tasmādyudhyasva bhārata 2-18
verses.colloquial:
antavanta ime dehaa nityasya uktaah shariirinah
anaashinah aprameyasya tasmaad yudhyasva bhaarata 2-18
verses.translation_reworded: These bodies that house the embodied Self are said to come to an end. But the Self is eternal, indestructible and beyond comprehension. So fight, Bharata.

verses.title: 2.19 ya enam vetti hantaram
verses.sanskrit:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥ २-१९॥
verses.roman:
ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate 2-19
verses.colloquial:
ya enam vetti hantaaram yash cha enam manyate hatam
ubhau tau na vijaaniito na ayam hanti na hanyate 2-19
verses.translation_reworded: Whoever thinks the Self kills, and whoever thinks It is killed, both lack understanding. The Self neither kills nor is killed.

verses.title: 2.20 na jayate mriyate
verses.sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्
नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥ २-२०॥
verses.roman:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin
nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo
na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre 2-20
verses.colloquial:
na jaayate mriyate vaa kadaachin
naayam bhuutvaa bhavitaa vaa na bhuuyah
ajo nityah shaashvatah ayam puraanah
na hanyate hanyamaane shariire 2-20
verses.translation_reworded: The Self is never born and never dies. Having once existed, It never stops existing. Unborn, eternal, unchanging and ancient, It is not killed when the body is killed.

verses.title: 2.21 vedavinashinam nityam
verses.sanskrit:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् ।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥ २-२१॥
verses.roman:
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam 2-21
verses.colloquial:
veda avinaashinam nityam ya enam ajam avyayam
katham sa purushah paartha kam ghaatayati hanti kam 2-21
verses.translation_reworded: Partha, how can anyone who knows the Self to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and inexhaustible kill anyone, or cause anyone to be killed?

verses.title: 2.22 vasansi jirnani yatha
verses.sanskrit:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय
नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा-
न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥ २-२२॥
verses.roman:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya
navāni gṛhṇāti naro'parāṇi
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇā-
nyanyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī 2-22
verses.colloquial:
vaasaamsi jiirnaani yathaa vihaaya
navaani grihnaati naro'paraani
tathaa shariiraani vihaaya jiirnaa-
ni anyaani samyaati navaani dehii 2-22
verses.translation_reworded: Just as a person discards worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the embodied Self discards worn-out bodies and takes on new ones.

verses.title: 2.23 nainam chhindanti
verses.sanskrit:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥ २-२३॥
verses.roman:
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ 2-23
verses.colloquial:
nainam chindanti shastraani nainam dahati paavakah
na chainam kledayanti aapah na shoshayati maarutah 2-23
verses.translation_reworded: Weapons cannot cut the Self, fire cannot burn It, water cannot wet It, and wind cannot dry It.

verses.title: 2.24 achchhedyo yam adahyo
verses.sanskrit:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च ।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥ २-२४॥
verses.roman:
acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ 2-24
verses.colloquial:
acchedyo' yam adaahyo' yam akledyo' shoshya eva cha
nityah sarva gatah sthaanur achalo' yam sanaatanah 2-24
verses.translation_reworded: This Self cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried. It is eternal, present everywhere, stable, unmoving and ancient.

verses.title: 2.25 avyakto yam achintyo
verses.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते ।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २-२५॥
verses.roman:
avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate
tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi 2-25
verses.colloquial:
avyakto'yam achintyo'yam avikaaryo'yam uchyate
tasmaad evam viditvaa enam naanushochitum arhasi 2-25
verses.translation_reworded: The Self is described as unmanifest, beyond thought, and unchangeable. Knowing It to be like this, you have no reason to grieve.

verses.title: 2.26 atha chainam nitya-jatam
verses.sanskrit:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २-२६॥
verses.roman:
atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam
tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitumarhasi 2-26
verses.colloquial:
atha chainam nitya jaatam nityam vaa manyase mritam
tathaapi tvam mahaa baaho naivam shochitum arhasi 2-26
verses.translation_reworded: And even if you believe the Self is born again and again and dies again and again, mighty-armed one, you still should not grieve.

verses.title: 2.27 jatasya hi dhruvo
verses.sanskrit:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २-२७॥
verses.roman:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca
tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi 2-27
verses.colloquial:
jaatasya hi dhruvo mrityur dhruvam janma mritasya cha
tasmaad aparihaarye'rthe na tvam shochitum arhasi 2-27
verses.translation_reworded: Whatever is born is certain to die, and whatever dies is certain to be born again. You should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.

verses.title: 2.28 avyaktadini bhutani
verses.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत ।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ २-२८॥
verses.roman:
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata
avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā 2-28
verses.colloquial:
avyakta aadiini bhuutaani vyakta madhyaani bhaarata
avyakta nidhanaani eva tatra kaa paridevanaa 2-28
verses.translation_reworded: Bharata, beings are unmanifest before they appear and unmanifest again after they end; only in between do they seem to be manifest. What is there in this to mourn?

verses.title: 2.29 ashcharya-vat pashyati
verses.sanskrit:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन-
माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः ।
आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श‍ृणोति
श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥ २-२९॥
verses.roman:
āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidena-
māścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ
āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti
śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit 2-29
verses.colloquial:
aashcharya vat pashyati kashchid ena-
maashcharya vat vadati tathaa eva cha anyah
aashcharya vat cha enam anyah shrinoti
shrutvaa api enam veda na cha eva kashchit 2-29
verses.translation_reworded: One person sees the Self as a marvel, another describes It as a marvel, another hears of It as a marvel; and yet, even after hearing, no one understands It at all.

verses.title: 2.30 dehi nityam avadhyo
verses.sanskrit:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत ।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २-३०॥
verses.roman:
dehī nityamavadhyo'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata
tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi 2-30
verses.colloquial:
dehii nityam avadhyo'yam dehe sarvasya bhaarata
tasmaat sarvaani bhuutaani na tvam shochitum arhasi 2-30
verses.translation_reworded: Bharata, the One who dwells in every body can never be destroyed. So you should not grieve for any living creature.

verses.title: 2.31 sva-dharmam api
verses.sanskrit:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि ।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥ २-३१॥
verses.roman:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi
dharmyāddhi yuddhācchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate 2-31
verses.colloquial:
svadharmam api cha avekshya na vikampitum arhasi
dharmyaat dhi yuddhaat shreyah anyat kshatriyasya na vidyate 2-31
verses.translation_reworded: Besides, when you consider your own duty, you should not hesitate, because for a Kshatriya there is nothing greater than a righteous war.

verses.title: 2.32 yadrichchhaya chopapannam
verses.sanskrit:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् ।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥ २-३२॥
verses.roman:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam 2-32
verses.colloquial:
yadricchayaa chopapannam svarga dvaaram apaavritam
sukhinah kshatriyaah paartha labhante yuddham iidrisham 2-32
verses.translation_reworded: Partha, fortunate are the Kshatriyas who are called to a battle like this one, which arrives on its own as an open gateway to heaven.

verses.title: 2.33 atha chet tvam imam
verses.sanskrit:
अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं सङ्ग्रामं न करिष्यसि ।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ २-३३॥
verses.roman:
atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṅgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi
tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi 2-33
verses.colloquial:
atha chet tvam imam dharmyam sangraamam na karishyasi
tatah svadharmam kiirtim cha hitvaa paapam avaapsyasi 2-33
verses.translation_reworded: But if you refuse to fight this righteous war, you will have thrown away both your duty and your honor, and you will fall into sin.

verses.title: 2.34 akirtim chapi bhutani
verses.sanskrit:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् ।
सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥ २-३४॥
verses.roman:
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te'vyayām
sambhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate 2-34
verses.colloquial:
akiirtim cha api bhuutaani kathayishyanti te'vyayaam
sambhaavitasya cha akiirtih maranaat atirichyate 2-34
verses.translation_reworded: People will also tell of your lasting disgrace, and for someone who has been honored, disgrace is worse than death.

verses.title: 2.35 bhayad ranad uparatam
verses.sanskrit:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः ।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥ २-३५॥
verses.roman:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam 2-35
verses.colloquial:
bhayaad ranaat uparatam mamsyante tvaam mahaarathaah
yeshaam cha tvam bahumato bhuutvaa yaasyasi laaghavam 2-35
verses.translation_reworded: The great commanders will assume you left the battle out of fear, and those who once held you and your heroism in high regard will look down on you.

verses.title: 2.36 avachya-vadansh cha
verses.sanskrit:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः ।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥ २-३६॥
verses.roman:
avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ
nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim 2-36
verses.colloquial:
avaachya vaadaamsh cha bahuun vadishyanti tava ahitaah
nindantah tava saamarthyam tato duhkhataram nu kim 2-36
verses.translation_reworded: Your enemies will say many things that should never be said, mocking your abilities. What could be more painful than that?

verses.title: 2.37 hato va prapsyasi
verses.sanskrit:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥ २-३७॥
verses.roman:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm
tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ 2-37
verses.colloquial:
hato vaa praapsyasi svargam jitvaa vaa bhokshyase mahiim
tasmaad uttishtha kaunteya yuddhaaya krita nishchayah 2-37
verses.translation_reworded: If you are killed, you will reach heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the earth. So stand up, son of Kunti, and resolve to fight.

verses.title: 2.38 sukha-duhkhe same
verses.sanskrit:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ २-३८॥
verses.roman:
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi 2-38
verses.colloquial:
sukha duhkhe same kritvaa laabha alaabhau jaya ajayau
tato yuddhaaya yujyasva na evam paapam avaapsyasi 2-38
verses.translation_reworded: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, and then engage in battle for the sake of battle. In this way you will not fall into sin.

verses.title: 2.39 esha te bhihita
verses.sanskrit:
एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श‍ृणु ।
बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥ २-३९॥
verses.roman:
eṣā te'bhihitā sāṅkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi 2-39
verses.colloquial:
eshaa te'bhihitaa saankhye buddhir yoge tvimaam shrinu
buddhyaa yukto yayaa paartha karma bandham prahaasyasi 2-39
verses.translation_reworded: What I have taught you so far is the wisdom of Sankhya. Now hear the wisdom of Yoga; once you know it, Partha, you will throw off the bonds of action.

verses.title: 2.40 nehabhikrama-nasho
verses.sanskrit:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥ २-४०॥
verses.roman:
nehābhikramanāśo'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate
svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt 2-40
verses.colloquial:
nehaabhikrama naasho'sti pratyavaayo na vidyate
svalpamapyasya dharmasya traayate mahato bhayaat 2-40
verses.translation_reworded: On this path no effort is wasted, and no harm (no contrary result) comes of it. Even a little of this knowledge, even a little practice of this Yoga, protects a person from the great fear.

verses.title: 2.41 vyavasayatmika buddhir
verses.sanskrit:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन ।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥ २-४१॥
verses.roman:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana
bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo'vyavasāyinām 2-41
verses.colloquial:
vyavasaaya aatmikaa buddhih eka iha kurunandana
bahu shaakhaa hi anantaah cha buddhayah avyavasaayinaam 2-41
verses.translation_reworded: Here, Kurunandana, joy of the Kurus, the resolve is single-pointed, while the thoughts of the irresolute branch out endlessly in every direction.

verses.title: 2.42 yamimam pushpitam
verses.sanskrit:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः ।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥ २-४२॥
verses.roman:
yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ 2-42
verses.colloquial:
yaam imaam pushpitaam vaacham pravadanti avipashchitah
veda vaadarataah paartha na anyat asti iti vaadinah 2-42
verses.translation_reworded: Partha, the unwise, who delight in the flattering words of the Vedas, make flowery speeches and declare that there is nothing beyond them.

verses.title: 2.43 kamatmanah svarga-para
verses.sanskrit:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् ।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥ २-४३॥
verses.roman:
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām
kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati 2-43
verses.colloquial:
kaamaatmaanah svargaparaa janma karma phala pradaam
kriyaa vishesha bahulaam bhoga aishvarya gatim prati 2-43
verses.translation_reworded: Driven by desire and aiming at heaven, they speak these flowery words, which promise rebirth as the reward of action and lay down many specific rituals for gaining pleasure and power.

verses.title: 2.44 bhogaisvarya-prasaktanam
verses.sanskrit:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥ २-४४॥
verses.roman:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate 2-44
verses.colloquial:
bhoga aishvarya prasaktaanaam tayaa apahrita chetasaam
vyavasaaya aatmikaa buddhih samaadhau na vidhiiyate 2-44
verses.translation_reworded: Those who cling to pleasure and power, and whose minds are carried away by such teaching, have no firm, single-pointed resolve, and they are not fit for steady meditation and samadhi.

verses.title: 2.45 trai-gunya-vishaya
verses.sanskrit:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥ २-४५॥
verses.roman:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna
nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān 2-45
verses.colloquial:
traigunya vishayaa vedaa nistraigunyo bhava arjuna
nirdvandvo nitya sattva stha niryoga kshema aatmavaan 2-45
verses.translation_reworded: The Vedas deal with the three qualities (gunas). Arjuna, rise above these three qualities, free yourself from the pairs of opposites, remain always in sattwa (goodness), let go of all concern with acquiring and holding on to things, and be established in the Self.

verses.title: 2.46 yavan artha udapane
verses.sanskrit:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके ।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥ २-४६॥
verses.roman:
yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake
tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ 2-46
verses.colloquial:
yaavaan artha udapaane sarvatah sampluta udake
taavaan sarveshu vedeshu braahmanasya vijaanatah 2-46
verses.translation_reworded: To the Brahmana who has known the Self, all the Vedas are of as much use as a water tank in a place that is flooded on every side.

verses.title: 2.47 karmany-evadhikaras
verses.sanskrit:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ २-४७॥
verses.roman:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana
mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi 2-47
verses.colloquial:
karmani eva adhikaarah te maa phaleshu kadaachana
maa karma phala hetuh bhuuh maa te sangah astu akarmani 2-47
verses.translation_reworded: You have a right only to your work, never to its results. Do not let the fruit of action be your motive, and do not let yourself become attached to inaction either.

verses.title: 2.48 yoga-sthah kuru karmani
verses.sanskrit:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ २-४८॥
verses.roman:
yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate 2-48
verses.colloquial:
yoga sthah kuru karmaani sangam tyaktvaa dhananjaya
siddhi asiddhyoh samah bhuutvaa samatvam yoga uchyate 2-48
verses.translation_reworded: Dhananjaya, act while giving up attachment, staying firm in Yoga, and remaining balanced in success and failure. This evenness of mind is what is called Yoga.

verses.title: 2.49 durena hy-avaram karma
verses.sanskrit:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय ।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥ २-४९॥
verses.roman:
dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanañjaya
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ 2-49
verses.colloquial:
duurena hyavaram karma buddhi yogaad dhananjaya
buddhau sharanam anviccha kripanaah phala hetavah 2-49
verses.translation_reworded: Dhananjaya, action is far inferior to the Yoga of wisdom. Take refuge in wisdom. Pitiable are those whose motive is the reward.

verses.title: 2.50 buddhi-yukto jahatiha
verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते ।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥ २-५०॥
verses.roman:
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam 2-50
verses.colloquial:
buddhi yukto jahaati iha ubhe sukrita dushkrite
tasmaad yogaaya yujyasva yogah karmasu kaushalam 2-50
verses.translation_reworded: Someone who has the wisdom of evenness of mind casts off both good and bad deeds in this very life. So devote yourself to Yoga. Skill in action is Yoga.

verses.title: 2.51 karma-jam buddhi-yukta
verses.sanskrit:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥ २-५१॥
verses.roman:
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ
janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam 2-51
verses.colloquial:
karmajam buddhi yuktaa hi phalam tyaktvaa maniishinah
janma bandha vinirmuktaah padam gacchanti anaamayam 2-51
verses.translation_reworded: The wise, possessing knowledge and having given up the fruits of their actions, are freed from the chains of birth and reach the State beyond all evil.

verses.title: 2.52 yada te moha-kalilam
verses.sanskrit:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥ २-५२॥
verses.roman:
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca 2-52
verses.colloquial:
yadaa te moha kalilam buddhir vyatitarishyati
tadaa gantaasi nirvedam shrotavyasya shrutasya cha 2-52
verses.translation_reworded: When your understanding has passed beyond the swamp of delusion, you will become indifferent to everything you have heard and everything you have yet to hear.

verses.title: 2.53 shruti-vipratipanna
verses.sanskrit:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला ।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥ २-५३॥
verses.roman:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā
samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi 2-53
verses.colloquial:
shruti vipratipannaa te yadaa sthaasyati nishchalaa
samaadhau achalaa buddhis tadaa yogam avaapsyasi 2-53
verses.translation_reworded: When your understanding, no longer unsettled by what you have heard, stands firm and steady in the Self, you will attain realization of the Self.

verses.title: 2.54 sthita-prajnasya ka
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच ।
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव ।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥ २-५४॥
verses.roman:
arjuna uvāca
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim 2-54
verses.colloquial:
arjuna uvaacha
sthita prajnasya kaa bhaashaa samaadhi sthasya keshava
sthita dhiih kim prabhaasheta kim aasiita vrajeta kim 2-54
verses.translation_reworded: Arjuna said: Keshava, how would you describe someone whose wisdom is steady and who is absorbed in the superconscious state? How does a person of steady wisdom speak, how does he sit, how does he walk?

verses.title: 2.55 prajahati yada kaman
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥ २-५५॥
verses.roman:
śrībhagavānuvāca
prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate 2-55
verses.colloquial:
shriibhagavaan uvaacha
prajahaati yadaa kaamaan sarvaan paartha manogataan
aatmani eva aatmanaa tushtah sthita prajnah tadaa uchyate 2-55
verses.translation_reworded: The Blessed Lord said: Partha, when a person completely gives up all the desires of the mind and is content in the Self through the Self alone, he is said to be one of steady wisdom.

verses.title: 2.56 duhkheshv-anudvigna-manah
verses.sanskrit:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥ २-५६॥
verses.roman:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate 2-56
verses.colloquial:
duhkheshu anudvigna manaah sukheshu vigata sprihah
viita raaga bhaya krodhah sthita dhiir munih uchyate 2-56
verses.translation_reworded: A person whose mind is not shaken by misfortune, who does not crave pleasures when things go well, and who is free of attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.

verses.title: 2.57 yah sarvatranabhisnehas
verses.sanskrit:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् ।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ २-५७॥
verses.roman:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā 2-57
verses.colloquial:
yah sarvatra anabhisnehas tattat praapya shubhaa ashubham
naabhinandati na dveshti tasya prajnaa pratishthitaa 2-57
verses.translation_reworded: One who is without attachment in every situation, who neither rejoices at what is good nor hates what is bad when it comes, has firmly established wisdom.

verses.title: 2.58 yada sanharate chayam
verses.sanskrit:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ २-५८॥
verses.roman:
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā 2-58
verses.colloquial:
yadaa samharate chaayam kuurmo'ngaaniiva sarvashah
indriyaanii indriyaarthebhyah tasya prajnaa pratishthitaa 2-58
verses.translation_reworded: When a person draws his senses back from their objects, just as a tortoise pulls its limbs in from every side, his wisdom becomes steady.

verses.title: 2.59 vishaya vinivartante
verses.sanskrit:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः ।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥ २-५९॥
verses.roman:
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ
rasavarjaṃ raso'pyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate 2-59
verses.colloquial:
vishayaa vinivartante niraahaarasya dehinah
rasa varjam raso'pyasya param drishtvaa nivartate 2-59
verses.translation_reworded: For someone who abstains, the objects of the senses fall away, but the longing for them stays behind. Even that longing disappears once he has seen the Supreme.

verses.title: 2.60 yatato hyapi kaunteya
verses.sanskrit:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥ २-६०॥
verses.roman:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ 2-60
verses.colloquial:
yatato hyapi kaunteya purushasya vipashchitah
indriyaani pramaathiini haranti prasabham manah 2-60
verses.translation_reworded: Son of Kunti, the restless senses forcibly drag away the mind even of a wise person who is striving to control them.

verses.title: 2.61 tani sarvani sanyamya
verses.sanskrit:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ २-६१॥
verses.roman:
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā 2-61
verses.colloquial:
taani sarvaani samyamya yukta aasiita matparah
vashe hi yasya indriyaani tasya prajnaa pratishthitaa 2-61
verses.translation_reworded: Once he has brought all the senses under control, he should sit firmly, with his mind fixed on Me. The person whose senses are mastered has wisdom that does not waver.

verses.title: 2.62 dhyayato vishayan
verses.sanskrit:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥ २-६२॥
verses.roman:
dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate
saṅgātsañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho'bhijāyate 2-62
verses.colloquial:
dhyaayato vishayaan pumsah sangas teshu upajaayate
sangaat sanjaayate kaamah kaamaat krodho'bhijaayate 2-62
verses.translation_reworded: When someone dwells on sense objects, attachment to them grows. Attachment gives rise to desire, and desire gives rise to anger.

verses.title: 2.63 krodhad bhavati sammohah
verses.sanskrit:
क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥ २-६३॥
verses.roman:
krodhādbhavati sammohaḥ sammohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ
smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati 2-63
verses.colloquial:
krodhaad bhavati sammohah sammohaat smriti vibhramah
smriti bhramshaad buddhi naasho buddhi naashaat pranashyati 2-63
verses.translation_reworded: Anger leads to delusion; delusion leads to loss of memory; loss of memory destroys the power of discrimination; and when discrimination is destroyed, the person is ruined.

verses.title: 2.64 raga-dvesha-viyuktais
verses.sanskrit:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् ।
आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥ २-६४॥
verses.roman:
rāgadveṣaviyuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran .
ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati 2-64
verses.colloquial:
raaga dvesha viyuktaih tu vishayaan indriyaih charan .
aatma vashyaih vidheya aatmaa prasaadam adhigacchati 2-64
verses.translation_reworded: But the self-controlled person who moves among sense objects with the senses held in check, free of both liking and disliking, reaches peace.

verses.title: 2.65 prasade sarva-duhkhanam
verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ २-६५॥
verses.roman:
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate
prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate 2-65
verses.colloquial:
prasaade sarva duhkhaanaam haanih asya upajaayate
prasanna chetasah hi aashu buddhih paryavatishthate 2-65
verses.translation_reworded: In that peace every sorrow comes to an end, because the understanding of a calm-minded person quickly becomes firm.

verses.title: 2.66 nasti buddhir-ayuktasya
verses.sanskrit:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥ २-६६॥
verses.roman:
nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā
na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham 2-66
verses.colloquial:
naasti buddhir ayuktasya na cha ayuktasya bhaavanaa
na cha abhaavayatah shaantih ashaantasya kutah sukham 2-66
verses.translation_reworded: Someone whose mind is unsteady has no knowledge of the Self, and no meditation. Without meditation there is no peace, and without peace, how could there be happiness?

verses.title: 2.67 indriyanam hi charatam
verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते ।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥ २-६७॥
verses.roman:
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano'nuvidhīyate
tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi 2-67
verses.colloquial:
indriyaanaam hi charataam yan manah anuvidhiiyate
tad asya harati prajnaam vaayuh naavam iva ambhasi 2-67
verses.translation_reworded: For when the mind runs after the roaming senses, it sweeps away a person's discrimination, just as the wind sweeps a boat across the water.

verses.title: 2.68 tasmad yasya maha-baho
verses.sanskrit:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ २-६८॥
verses.roman:
tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā 2-68
verses.colloquial:
tasmaad yasya mahaa baaho nigrihiitaani sarvashah
indriyaaniindriya arthebhyah tasya prajnaa pratishthitaa 2-68
verses.translation_reworded: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, the person whose senses are fully withdrawn from sense objects has knowledge that is firm.

verses.title: 2.69 ya nisha sarva-bhutanam
verses.sanskrit:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥ २-६९॥
verses.roman:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ 2-69
verses.colloquial:
yaa nishaa sarva bhuutaanaam tasyaam jaagarti samyamii
yasyaam jaagrati bhuutaani saa nishaa pashyatah muneh 2-69
verses.translation_reworded: What is night for all other beings is the time when the self-controlled person is awake; and the time when all beings are awake is night for the sage (muni) who truly sees.

verses.title: 2.70 apuryamanam achala
verses.sanskrit:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं
समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे
स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥ २-७०॥
verses.roman:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ
samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve
sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī 2-70
verses.colloquial:
aapuuryamaanam achala pratishtham
samudram aapah pravishanti yadvat
tadvat kaamaa yam pravishanti sarve
sa shaantim aapnoti na kaama kaamii 2-70
verses.translation_reworded: The person into whom all desires flow, as rivers flow into the ocean that is filled from every side yet stays unmoved, reaches peace. The one who chases desires does not.

verses.title: 2.71 vihaya kaman yah sarvan
verses.sanskrit:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥ २-७१॥
verses.roman:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati 2-71
verses.colloquial:
vihaaya kaamaan yah sarvaan pumaan charati nihsprihah
nirmamah nirahankaarah sa shaantim adhigacchati 2-71
verses.translation_reworded: The person who gives up all desires and lives without craving, without any sense of 'I' or 'mine', reaches peace.

verses.title: 2.72 esha brahmi sthitih
verses.sanskrit:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥ २-७२॥ 

ॐ तत्सदिति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु
ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे श्रीकृष्णार्जुनसंवादे
साङ्ख्ययोगो नाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः ॥ २॥
verses.roman:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati 
sthitvāsyāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati 2-72

oṃ tatsaditi śrīmadbhagavadgītāsūpaniṣatsu
brahmavidyāyāṃ yogaśāstre śrīkṛṣṇārjunasaṃvāde
sāṅkhyayogo nāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ 2
verses.colloquial:
eshaa braahmii sthitih paartha nainaam praapya vimuhyati
sthitvaa asyaam antakaale'pi brahma nirvaanam ricchati

om tatsad iti shriimad bhagavad giitaasu upanishatsu
brahma vidyaayaam yoga shaastre shrii krishna arjuna samvaade
saankhya yogo naama dvitiiyo'dhyaayah 2
verses.translation_reworded:
This is the state of Brahman, O son of Pritha. Whoever reaches it is no longer deluded. Established in it, even at the moment of death, a person attains oneness with Brahman.

So ends the second discourse, called "The Yoga of Knowledge," in the Upanishads of the glorious Bhagavad Gita, the science of the Eternal, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna.
